Breast Cancer Classification Add On: More Penalization methods.

Biostatistics 735/794 — Machine Learning in Public Health (R)

Alexander McLain

September 18, 2025

  • Loading in the data
  • Logistic Lasso (glmnet)
  • Logistic Ridge (glmnet)
  • Logistic SCAD/MCP (ncvreg)

# Core
library(tidyverse)
library(rsample)
library(recipes)
library(yardstick)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Models
library(glmnet)        # logistic lasso/ridge
library(ncvreg)        # For scad/mcp

# Metrics
library(pROC)          # CI's for prediction metrics

Loading in the data

Data: Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC)

Each row is a patient. Outcome is diagnosis: Malignant (M) or Benign (B).

There are 30 numeric features computed from a digitized image of a breast mass (10 characteristics × 3 summaries: mean, standard error, “worst”).

# Download from UCI ML repo
  url_data  <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/breast-cancer-wisconsin/wdbc.data"
  raw <- read.csv(url_data, header = FALSE)


# According to UCI:
# V1 = ID, V2 = Diagnosis (M/B), V3:V32 = 30 features
names(raw) <- c("ID","Diagnosis",
                "radius_mean","texture_mean","perimeter_mean","area_mean","smoothness_mean",
                "compactness_mean","concavity_mean","concave_points_mean","symmetry_mean","fractal_dimension_mean",
                "radius_se","texture_se","perimeter_se","area_se","smoothness_se",
                "compactness_se","concavity_se","concave_points_se","symmetry_se","fractal_dimension_se",
                "radius_worst","texture_worst","perimeter_worst","area_worst","smoothness_worst",
                "compactness_worst","concavity_worst","concave_points_worst","symmetry_worst","fractal_dimension_worst")

bc <- raw %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(Diagnosis = factor(Diagnosis, levels = c("B","M"))) %>%  # B=negative (benign), M=positive (malignant)
  select(-ID)

glimpse(bc)

We’ll create a train/test split once, then do model selection and evaluation within the training set (for AIC/BIC and CV). The test set is reserved for a final sanity check (optional).

set.seed(42)
split <- initial_split(bc, prop = 0.8, strata = Diagnosis)
train <- training(split)
test  <- testing(split)

nrow(train); nrow(test)
## [1] 454
## [1] 115

Preprocessing Recipe

Before commensing with the CV, we’re going to create some functions to help us scale/center predictors and keep the outcome as a factor. This avoids leakage by fitting the recipe inside resamples when used with rsample.

rec_base <- recipe(Diagnosis ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors())
prep_base <- prep(rec_base)         # for direct train fit (non-CV steps)
train_ready <- bake(prep_base, train)
test_ready  <- bake(prep_base, test)

Logistic Lasso (glmnet)

We fit a penalized logistic regression (lasso) with internal CV to choose (\(\lambda\)). Then evaluate on the test set.

# Rebuild design matrices from the preprocessed data
x_tr <- model.matrix(Diagnosis ~ . - 1, data = train_ready)
y_tr <- train_ready$Diagnosis

x_te <- model.matrix(Diagnosis ~ . - 1, data = test_ready)
y_te <- test_ready$Diagnosis

set.seed(202)
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1, family = "binomial", 
                      nfolds = 10, type.measure = "class")
plot(cv_lasso)

lam_min  <- cv_lasso$lambda.min
lam_1se  <- cv_lasso$lambda.1se

fit_min <- glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1, family = "binomial", lambda = lam_min)
fit_1se <- glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1, family = "binomial", lambda = lam_1se)


tibble(
  Variable = rownames(coef(fit_min))[-1],
  coef_min = coef(fit_min)[-1],
  coef_1se = coef(fit_1se)[-1], 
) %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "Coefficient estimates for Logistic Lasso (note: all X and standardized).")

tibble(
  model = c("Lasso (min)","Lasso (1SE)"),
  AUC   = c(roc_auc_vec(y_te, p_min, event_level = "second"),
            roc_auc_vec(y_te, p_1se, event_level = "second")),

Logistic Ridge (glmnet)

We fit a penalized ridge regression (ridge) with internal CV to choose (\(\lambda\)). Then evaluate on the test set.

# Rebuild design matrices from the preprocessed data
x_tr <- model.matrix(Diagnosis ~ . - 1, data = train_ready)
y_tr <- train_ready$Diagnosis

x_te <- model.matrix(Diagnosis ~ . - 1, data = test_ready)
y_te <- test_ready$Diagnosis

set.seed(202)
cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0, family = "binomial", 
                      nfolds = 10, type.measure = "class")
plot(cv_ridge)

lam_min  <- cv_ridge$lambda.min
lam_1se  <- cv_ridge$lambda.1se

fit_min_ridge <- glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0, family = "binomial", lambda = lam_min)
fit_1se_ridge <- glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0, family = "binomial", lambda = lam_1se)

p_min_ridge <- predict(fit_min_ridge, newx = x_te, type = "response")[,1]
p_1se_ridge <- predict(fit_1se_ridge, newx = x_te, type = "response")[,1]

cls_min_ridge <- factor(ifelse(p_min_ridge >= 0.5, "M","B"), levels = levels(y_te))
cls_1se_ridge <- factor(ifelse(p_1se_ridge >= 0.5, "M","B"), levels = levels(y_te))


tibble(
  model = c("Ridge (min)","Ridge (1SE)"),
  AUC   = c(roc_auc_vec(y_te, p_min_ridge, event_level = "second"),
            roc_auc_vec(y_te, p_1se_ridge, event_level = "second")),
  Spec  = c(spec_vec(y_te, cls_min_ridge, event_level = "second"),
            spec_vec(y_te, cls_1se_ridge, event_level = "second")),
  NPV   = c(npv_vec(y_te, cls_min_ridge, event_level = "second"),
            npv_vec(y_te, cls_1se_ridge, event_level = "second"))
) %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "Test-set performance: Logistic with Ridge penalty")%>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

Logistic SCAD/MCP (ncvreg)

We fit a penalized logistic regression (SCAD/MCP) with internal CV to choose (\(\lambda\)). Then evaluate on the test set.

# Rebuild design matrices from the preprocessed data
x_tr <- model.matrix(Diagnosis ~ . - 1, data = train_ready)
y_tr <- train_ready$Diagnosis

x_te <- model.matrix(Diagnosis ~ . - 1, data = test_ready)
y_te <- test_ready$Diagnosis

set.seed(202)
cv_mcp <- cv.ncvreg(x_tr, y_tr, penalty = "MCP",  family = "binomial", nfolds = 10)
plot(cv_mcp)

set.seed(202)
cv_scad <- cv.ncvreg(x_tr, y_tr, penalty = "SCAD",  family = "binomial", nfolds = 10)
plot(cv_scad)

tibble(
  Variable = rownames(coef(fit_min))[-1],
  coef_mcp = coef(cv_mcp)[-1],
  coef_scad = coef(cv_scad)[-1], 
) %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "Coefficient estimates for Logistic MCP and SCAD models.")%>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

Confidence Intervals for prediction metrics

It is common to want confidence intervals for AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. These can be obtained for any given model. Below, we’ll focus on the lasso model with 1se rule for selecting \(\lambda\).

First, we’ll use the pROC package to get CI’s for AUC, sensitivity, and specificity.

# truth: factor with levels 
# prob: predicted probability for the positive class
truth <- test_ready$Diagnosis
roc_obj <- roc(response = truth, predictor = p_1se, levels = c("B","M"), direction = "<")

# AUC + 95% CI (DeLong by default)
auc(roc_obj)
## Area under the curve: 0.999
ci.auc(roc_obj)                 # (lower, AUC, upper)
## 95% CI: 0.9969-1 (DeLong)
# Sensitivity/Specificity CI 
ci.se.obj <- ci.se(roc_obj)
plot(roc_obj) # restart a new plot
plot(ci.se.obj, col="blue")

ci.se.obj 
## 95% CI (2000 stratified bootstrap replicates):
##   sp se.low se.median se.high
##  0.0 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.1 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.2 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.3 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.4 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.5 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.6 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.7 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.8 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.9 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  1.0 0.8605    0.9535       1
ci.sp.obj <- ci.sp(roc_obj)
plot(roc_obj) # restart a new plot
plot(ci.sp.obj, col="blue")

ci.sp.obj
## 95% CI (2000 stratified bootstrap replicates):
##   se sp.low sp.median sp.high
##  0.0 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.1 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.2 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.3 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.4 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.5 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.6 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.7 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.8 1.0000    1.0000       1
##  0.9 0.9722    1.0000       1
##  1.0 0.9583    0.9861       1
# Alternatively: CI along the ROC curve at fixed specificity/sensitivity targets
# Here, we'll use the specificity/sensitivity at a threshold of 0.5.
thr <- 0.5
spec <- roc_obj$specificities[which.max(roc_obj$thresholds > 0.5)]
ci.se(roc_obj, specificities = spec)
## 95% CI (2000 stratified bootstrap replicates):
##         sp se.low se.median se.high
##  0.9861111 0.8837         1       1
sens <- roc_obj$sensitivities[which.max(roc_obj$thresholds > 0.5)]
ci.sp(roc_obj, sensitivities = sens)
## 95% CI (2000 stratified bootstrap replicates):
##         se sp.low sp.median sp.high
##  0.9767442 0.9583    0.9931       1

Second, we’ll use bootstrapping to get CI’s for all of our prediction metrics. There are other ways we could get CI’s for sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV since they just proportions. However, using bootstrapping gives use some extra flexibility. For example, if we were using Youden’s Index to select our threshold, we could embed the selection of it into our bootstrapping. This would result in CI’s that account for the uncertainty in the selected threshold.

boot_ci_metrics <- function(truth, prob, thr = 0.5, B = 2000, levels) {
  # The first element of "levels" must correspond to a "high" prob.
  truth <- factor(truth, levels = levels)
  n <- length(truth)
  stat <- function(idx) {
    tr <- truth[idx]; pr <- prob[idx]
    pred <- factor(ifelse(pr >= thr, levels[1], levels[2]), levels = levels(tr))
    TP <- sum(tr==levels[1] & pred==levels[1]); FP <- sum(tr==levels[2] & pred==levels[1])
    FN <- sum(tr==levels[1] & pred==levels[2]); TN <- sum(tr==levels[2] & pred==levels[2])
    se <- ifelse(TP+FN>0, TP/(TP+FN), NA)
    sp <- ifelse(TN+FP>0, TN/(TN+FP), NA)
    ppv<- ifelse(TP+FP>0, TP/(TP+FP), NA)
    npv<- ifelse(TN+FN>0, TN/(TN+FN), NA)
    auc<- tryCatch(as.numeric(auc(roc(tr, pr, levels=c(levels[2],levels[1]), direction="<"))),
                   error=function(e) NA)
    c(auc=auc, se=se, sp=sp, ppv=ppv, npv=npv)
  }
  S <- stat(seq_len(n))
  M <- replicate(B, stat(sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)))
  ci <- apply(M, 1, function(x) quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE))
tribble(~value,~auc, ~se, ~sp, ~ppv, ~npv, 
        "Estimates", S[1], S[2], S[3], S[4], S[5],
        "CI_95_L", ci[1,1], ci[1,2], ci[1,3], ci[1,4], ci[1,5],
        "CI_95_U", ci[2,1], ci[2,2], ci[2,3], ci[2,4], ci[2,5]
                 )
}

set.seed(1)
out <- boot_ci_metrics(truth, p_1se, thr = 0.5, B = 2000, levels = c("M", "B"))
out %>%  kable(digits = 3)%>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
value auc se sp ppv npv
Estimates 0.999 0.977 0.986 0.977 0.986
CI_95_L 0.996 0.921 0.954 0.918 0.955
CI_95_U 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000
